newsitem.title: CHILE: Escondida union recommends ending strike.
newsitem.headline: Escondida union recommends ending strike.

text.p: The leadership of the workers union at Escondida copper mine has recommended to workers that they vote to accept a company pay offer and return to work in a vote Wednesday, a union leader said.
"The leadership recommends that they accept the pay offer," said Pablo Godoy, a leader of the 350-member union, by telephone from union headquarters in the northern city of Antofagasta.
"The workers will have the last word," he said, but the recommendation plainly indicated that support for the strike had evaporated.
The 800,000-tonne-a-year mine is owned by Broken Hill Proprietary and RTZ Corp plc.
The mine's some-350 unionized workers began a strike Friday to demand progress in wage negotiations. The rest of the mine's workforce of about 2,000 people did not join the strike.
